To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DAVIS dataset is a comprehensive benchmark for video object segmentation, that current approaches are not yet able to fully exploit the potential of deep convolutional networks and that the proposed metrics are well suited for evaluating and comparing the results of video object segmentation algorithms.

(1) the proposed DAVIS dataset is the most comprehensive video object segmentation dataset to date, (2) the proposed evaluation methodology is the most accurate one to date, (3) the current state-of-the-art approaches are not able to handle the challenges of the proposed dataset, (4) the proposed benchmark dataset will be a valuable tool for future research in the area of video segmentation, and (5) the proposed evaluation method will be a valuable metric for comparing and evaluating video object segmentation methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new benchmark dataset for video object segmentation, which we believe will be of interest and benefit to the computer vision community at large, and in particular to the research community focusing on video object segmentation.
